summary: This program adds a can_walk method to the RobotPet class, which reports whether a pet has enough battery for a walk of any length you ask about. Three pets are created and each is checked for a 30-minute walk.

lines.text: A method is a function that lives inside a class. Like __init__, its first parameter is self, so the method can look at the attributes of whichever pet it was called on; duration is the value you pass in when you call it.

This is the rule Frederick's shop uses: each minute of walking costs two ticks of battery. Because the duration arrives as a parameter, the same method answers the question for a 5-minute stroll or an hour-long hike.

The comparison itself evaluates to True or False, and return hands that answer back to whoever called the method. Nothing is printed here — a method that returns a value leaves the printing to the caller.
Calling the method on pet1 with the dot means Rover is the self inside can_walk, so his own battery is the one checked. The returned True or False is dropped straight into the f-string.
The \n is an escape sequence for a newline, so this prints a blank line before the heading and separates the two blocks of output.
